description:
FILED s446l (agent L) while probing #525; PRE-EXISTING, silent wrong, #138 family
(a statement's assignment half deleted with no announcement).

REPRO (perl vs ./runpcl):
  no strict 'refs';
  package H; our $tag = "H";
  sub inner { return ${"tag"} }
  sub loc   { local ${"tag"}    = "L"; return inner() }
  sub locq  { local ${"H::tag"} = "Q"; return inner() }
  package main;
  print H::loc(), "|", H::locq(), "|", $H::tag, "\n";
perl: L|Q|H     PCL: ||H
Also at file top level: `{ local ${"tag"} = "T"; ... }` reads undef inside.
The RESTORE half is correct -- only the new VALUE is lost.

CAUSE (located, emitted CL is the evidence):
  (p-local-deref-scalar "tag"
    <body>)
the `= "L"` is nowhere in the output.  Pl/Parser.pm ~3866 matches
`@non_ws >= 2` on Cast + Block/Symbol, emits the macro from those TWO
tokens and RETURNS -- everything after them, the `=` and its expression, is
discarded without a drop announcement.  The runtime macro is right: it saves
the box, clears it to nil, runs the body, restores (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
~14681).  Clearing to nil is what makes the read come back empty.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: Pl/t/local-symref-01.t covers exactly this family but
every row spells it `local ${aa};` and assigns on the NEXT statement, so the
initializer form was never exercised.  Add rows to that file.

FIX SHAPE: after the Cast+Block/Symbol pair, if the remaining tokens are
`= EXPR`, emit the assignment as the FIRST form of the macro body (the box is
resolved by then): scalar -> a p-setf through the same ref, array/hash -> the
list-assign forms.  Anything else left over must be LOUD (rule 12 /
announce), not silently dropped -- that silence is the actual defect.
Note the array/hash twins have the same shape and the same gap:
`local @{"n"} = (1,2)` and `local %{"n"} = (k=>1)` -- probe all three.

BAR: the repro + the qualified spelling + top level + all three sigils + the
no-initializer form (must not move) + `local $$ref = V` (hard ref still dies);
Pl/ change so corpus-diff + emission-ab, and `local` is in the sweep's path.
subject: `local ${"n"} = VALUE` SILENTLY DROPS the initializer -- the localized variable is cleared to undef and the assignment never happens (all three sigils, qualified and unqualified)
